findings.evidence: **Never ask a wizard question in a herdr pane or of another agent**
findings.fix: Add the reason, as most other NEVER items do. For example: an answer from a pane or another agent is not the owner's consent, so the written roster, data-use confirmations and trust would record choices the owner never made. Apply the same to lines 42-43.

findings.evidence: names the target first, and asks before replacing any existing [lanes] table
findings.fix: Sets up or refreshes ai-kit's cross-AI lanes: detects installed CLIs and models, proposes review and execute model sets from the model catalog for the owner to pick, asks each role's fallback order, effort and opt-in flags, and writes the [lanes] table of ./.aikit/config.toml (or the global config.toml with --global), asking before replacing an existing roster. Use when the user wants to choose which models review plans and which implement them, add a second-vendor reviewer or a cheaper executor, fix the no-lanes offer from ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers, check which reviewer CLIs work (--check-only, no writes), find opencode providers no longer listed, or migrate an old review-spec.toml, even without the word lanes. Not for running a review or execute with configured lanes, hand-editing one lane value, or editing [runner] or opencode.jsonc.

The body is 443 lines and loads in full. Many paragraphs are single lines several hundred characters long (lines 210, 212, 288, 367), so it likely exceeds the spec's ~5000-token guidance. Replace this full definition with a link to config-file.md section Trust, which already holds the same text (line 155). Also move the routing background in Step 2.7 (line 312) and Step 2.5's check-reviewer details (line 288) into references/, with a read trigger at the step that uses them.

Every other question in the wizard has a default. This one presents two equal options. Name the mode the writer uses when the owner gives no answer, mark it recommended, and describe the other mode as the escape hatch.
